newsitem.title: USA: Chevron says wins blocks offshore Australia.
newsitem.headline: Chevron says wins blocks offshore Australia.

text.p: Chevron Corp on Wednesday announced it won the right to explore three offshore areas for oil and natural gas in western Australia.
The three exploratory blocks are adjacent to Chevron-held areas where significant gas or oil discoveries have been made.
"With the new acreage, one of Chevron's largest deep water portfolios is now located in Australia," said Richard Matzke, president of Chevron Overseas Petroleum Inc.
Chevron will acquire a 25 percent interest in all three blocks from the Australian government.
Chevron said the new blocks have the potential to add significantly to Chevron's portfolio in Australia.
Chevron will acquire a 25 percent interest in Exploration Permits W96-4 and W96-5, which are located in the Browse Basin offshore North West Australia.
The blocks cover approximately 1.1 million acres (4,400 square kilometers) and are located 80 miles offshore, the company said.

The oil giant also holds a 25 percent interest in the adjacent block, Permit WA-241-P, where the recently drilled Cornea wells have discovered a potentially significant oil reservoir, the company said.
Delineation drilling in the newly acquired permit is planned for later this year to confimr if oil lies there.
Exploration Block W96-14 is located west of the gas-rich Gorgon/Chrysaor/Dionysus tract in the Carnarvon Basin, which could hold up to 15 trillion cubic feet of gas, the company said.

W96-14 covers approximately 1.4 million acres (5,500 square kilometers) and is located 100 miles offshore Western Australia. A drilling program is currently being planned, but the company declined to give a specific timeline.
